# Appendix: Proofs {#sec-appendix .appendix}

## Proof of @prp-moments {#sec-proof-moments}

For the binary distribution, the moments are just averages over the two types:

$$
\kappa^B=\frac{1}{2u_\ell}+\frac{1}{2u_H},
\qquad
\nu^B=\frac{u_\ell+u_H}{2},
\qquad
\lambda^B=\frac{1}{2u_\ell^2}+\frac{1}{2u_H^2}.
$$

For the uniform distribution, the density is

$$
f(v)=\frac{1}{2\delta}\mathbf{1}_{[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta]}(v).
$$

Direct integration gives

$$
\kappa^U
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\int_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}v^{-1/2}\,dv
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\cdot\bigl[2\sqrt v\bigr]_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}
=\frac{u_H-u_\ell}{\delta}.
$$

Similarly,

$$
\nu^U
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\int_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}v^{1/2}\,dv
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\cdot\left[\frac{2}{3}v^{3/2}\right]_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}
=\frac{u_H^3-u_\ell^3}{3\delta}.
$$

For $\lambda^U$,

$$
\lambda^U
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\int_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}v^{-1}\,dv
=\frac{1}{2\delta}\cdot\bigl[\ln v\bigr]_{\mu-\delta}^{\mu+\delta}
=\frac{\ln(\mu+\delta)-\ln(\mu-\delta)}{2\delta}
=\frac{\ln(u_H^2/u_\ell^2)}{2\delta}
=\frac{\ln(u_H/u_\ell)}{\delta}.
$$

To compare $\kappa^B$ and $\kappa^U$, use the strict convexity of $v^{-1/2}$. Jensen's inequality gives

$$
\kappa^B=\E_{\mathrm{binary}}[V_L^{-1/2}]
>
\left(\E_{\mathrm{binary}}[V_L]\right)^{-1/2}
=\mu^{-1/2}.
$$

Also, since $u_H^2-u_\ell^2=2\delta$,

$$
\kappa^U=\frac{u_H-u_\ell}{\delta}=\frac{2}{u_H+u_\ell},
\qquad
\kappa^B=\frac{1}{2u_\ell}+\frac{1}{2u_H}
=\frac{u_H+u_\ell}{2u_\ell u_H}.
$$

Thus

$$
\kappa^B-\kappa^U
=\frac{(u_H+u_\ell)^2-4u_\ell u_H}{2u_\ell u_H(u_H+u_\ell)}
=\frac{(u_H-u_\ell)^2}{2u_\ell u_H(u_H+u_\ell)}
>0.
$$

Hence $\kappa^B>\kappa^U$.

## Proof of @prp-ss {#sec-proof-ss}

We seek a Bayesian Nash equilibrium $(x_M^*,\,x_L^*(\cdot))$ in which management chooses a constant $x_M^*$ and labor responds type-by-type. By @eq-brl, labor's best response to $x_M^*$ for type $v$ is

$$
x_L^*(v)=\sqrt{vx_M^*}-x_M^*.
$$

For management, given labor's equilibrium strategy, the first-order condition is

$$
V\cdot\E\!\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x_M}\frac{x_M}{x_L^*(V_L)+x_M}\right]=1.
$$

Equivalently, holding $x_L$ fixed in @eq-um,

$$
\frac{\partial U_M}{\partial x_M}=\frac{x_L}{(x_L+x_M)^2}V-1.
$$

At equilibrium, $x_L=x_L^*(v)=\sqrt{vx_M^*}-x_M^*$ and $x_L+x_M^*=\sqrt{vx_M^*}$. Taking expectations over types gives

$$
V\cdot\E\!\left[\frac{\sqrt{V_Lx_M^*}-x_M^*}{V_Lx_M^*}\right]=1.
$$

Simplifying,

$$
\begin{aligned}
V\!\left(
\frac{1}{\sqrt{x_M^*}}\E[V_L^{-1/2}]
-\E[V_L^{-1}]
\right)
&=V\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{x_M^*}}-\lambda\right)\\
&=1,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\lambda\equiv\E[V_L^{-1}]$. Solving for $\sqrt{x_M^*}$:

$$
\sqrt{x_M^*}=\frac{V\kappa}{1+V\lambda},
\qquad
x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}=\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}.
$$

The second-order condition for management is

$$
-V\cdot\E\!\left[\frac{x_L^*(V_L)}{(x_L^*(V_L)+x_M)^{3/2}}\right]\cdot\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x_M}}<0,
$$

which holds because $x_L^*(v)\ge 0$. Hence $x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}$ is the unique equilibrium management effort.

Substituting into @eq-brl,

$$
x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)
=\frac{V\kappa\sqrt{v}}{1+V\lambda}-\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}.
$$

The total effort is

$$
x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)+x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}
=\frac{V\kappa\sqrt{v}}{1+V\lambda}.
$$

Substituting into @eq-ul and @eq-um:

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)
&=\frac{x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)}
        {x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)+x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}}v
  -x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)\\
&=\left(1-\frac{V\kappa}{(1+V\lambda)\sqrt{v}}\right)v
  -\left(\frac{V\kappa\sqrt{v}}{1+V\lambda}
  -\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}\right)\\
&=\left(\sqrt{v}-\frac{V\kappa}{1+V\lambda}\right)^2,
\\[1.25ex]
U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)
&=\frac{x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}}
        {x_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)+x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}}V
  -x_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\\
&=\frac{V\kappa}{(1+V\lambda)\sqrt{v}}\,V
  -\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}\\
&=\frac{V^2\kappa}{(1+V\lambda)\sqrt{v}}
  -\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Taking expectations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]
&=\E\!\left[
v-\frac{2V\kappa\sqrt{v}}{1+V\lambda}
+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}
\right]\\
&=\mu-\frac{2V\kappa\nu}{1+V\lambda}
+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2},
\\[1.25ex]
\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]
&=\frac{V^2\kappa}{1+V\lambda}\E[V_L^{-1/2}]
  -\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}\\
&=\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{1+V\lambda}
  -\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}\\
&=\frac{V^3\kappa^2\lambda}{(1+V\lambda)^2}. \qquad\square
\end{aligned}
$$

## Proof of @prp-ml {#sec-proof-ml}
In ML, management commits first. Labor observes $x_M$ and best-responds type-by-type with $x_L^*(x_M;v)=\sqrt{vx_M}-x_M$, which management anticipates. Management therefore maximizes

$$
\E\!\left[U_M(x_L^*(V_L),x_M;V)\right]
=\E\!\left[V\sqrt{\frac{x_M}{V_L}}-x_M\right]
=V\sqrt{x_M}\,\kappa-x_M.
$$

This is the Stackelberg leader objective. The first- and second-order conditions are

$$
\frac{V\kappa}{2\sqrt{x_M}}-1=0,
\qquad
-\frac{V\kappa}{4x_M^{3/2}}<0,
$$

giving the unique maximizer $x_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=V^2\kappa^2/4$. Then @eq-brl implies

$$
x_L^{\mathrm{ML}}(v)=\frac{V\kappa}{2}\sqrt{v}-\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4},
\qquad
x_L^{\mathrm{ML}}(v)+x_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=\frac{V\kappa}{2}\sqrt{v}.
$$

Substituting into @eq-ul and @eq-um:

$$
U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}(v)=\left(\sqrt{v}-\frac{V\kappa}{2}\right)^2,
\qquad
U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}(v)=\frac{V^2\kappa}{2\sqrt{v}}-\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}.
$$

Taking expectations:

$$
\E[U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}]=\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4},
\qquad
\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]=\frac{V^2\kappa}{2}\cdot\kappa-\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}=\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}.
$$

Note the difference from the corrected SS: $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]=V^2\kappa^2/4$ while $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]=V^3\kappa^2\lambda/(1+V\lambda)^2$. They differ unless $V\lambda=1$. $\square$

## Proof of @prp-separating {#sec-proof-separating}

Labor solves

$$
\max_{x_L\ge 0}\;W(x_L;v)=\max_{x_L\ge 0}\left(\frac{v}{\sqrt V}\sqrt{x_L}-x_L\right).
$$

The first-order condition is

$$
\frac{v}{2\sqrt{Vx_L}} - 1 = 0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
x_L^{\mathrm{LM}}(v)=\frac{v^2}{4V}.
$$

The second-order condition is

$$
\frac{\partial^2 W}{\partial x_L^2}=-\frac{v}{4\sqrt V}x_L^{-3/2}<0,
$$

so this is the unique global optimum. Then @eq-brm implies

$$
x_M^{\mathrm{LM}}(v)
=\sqrt{V\cdot\frac{v^2}{4V}}-\frac{v^2}{4V}
=\frac{v(2V-v)}{4V}.
$$

Substituting into @eq-ul and @eq-um yields @eq-ul-lm and @eq-um-lm.

## Proof of @prp-no-pool {#sec-proof-no-pool}

The proof has two steps.

First, show that equilibrium effort is one-to-one in type. Define

$$
\phi:[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta]\to\mathbb{R},
\qquad
\phi(v)=\frac{v^2}{4V}.
$$

Because $\mu>\delta>0$, the support $[\mu-\delta,\mu+\delta]$ lies in $(0,\infty)$. Hence, for every $v$ in the support,

$$
\phi'(v)=\frac{v}{2V}>0.
$$

Therefore $\phi$ is strictly increasing on the support and thus injective. Equivalently, if $v\neq v'$, then

$$
\phi(v)\neq \phi(v').
$$

So distinct types cannot share the same optimal effort. Any candidate strategy that assigns the same effort to two different types is incompatible with the injectivity of $\phi$.

Second, prove strict global incentive compatibility of truthful play. Fix any true type $v$ and any $s\neq v$. If type $v$ chooses the effort associated with type $s$,

$$
x_L=\frac{s^2}{4V},
$$

then, after management responds according to @eq-brm, type $v$ obtains

$$
\tilde{U}(v,s)
=\frac{v}{\sqrt{V}}\cdot\frac{s}{2\sqrt{V}}-\frac{s^2}{4V}
=\frac{2vs-s^2}{4V}.
$$

Truthful play yields

$$
U(v,v)=\frac{v^2}{4V}.
$$

The payoff difference is

$$
U(v,v)-\tilde{U}(v,s)
=\frac{v^2-2vs+s^2}{4V}
=\frac{(v-s)^2}{4V}>0
\qquad\forall s\neq v.
$$

This difference is a positive-definite quadratic form and is strictly positive for every $s\neq v$. Hence any strategy that asks type $v$ to choose $s^2/(4V)$ with $s\neq v$ is strictly dominated by truthful play.

In the binary-type special case, this condition corresponds exactly to the main-text constraints $\text{IC}_{H}$ and $\text{IC}_{L}$. Those two constraints jointly are necessary and sufficient for the separating candidate to be feasible. Necessity follows because a separating equilibrium must rule out imitation in both directions. Sufficiency follows because, given the continuation best response in @eq-brm, once both IC constraints hold, each type optimally chooses its own action.

Let

$$
D(v,s)\equiv U(v,v)-\tilde U(v,s)=\frac{(v-s)^2}{4V}.
$$

For fixed $s$, $D(v,s)$ is zero only at $v=s$, and

$$
\frac{\partial D(v,s)}{\partial v}=\frac{v-s}{2V}
$$

changes sign at that point. This gives the single-crossing representation. But no separate single-crossing argument is needed here, because $D(v,s)>0$ for every $s\neq v$ already delivers the stronger global strict IC result.

Because management's continuation best response depends only on observed effort and the parameter $V$, not on posterior beliefs, beliefs cannot overturn this deviation argument. Therefore no pooling or semi-separating behavior can arise in PBE, and there is no parameter region in which pooling is feasible. The LM subgame admits a unique PBE, and it is separating.

## Proof of the LM Expected-Payoff Formulas {#sec-proof-lm-payoff}

From @eq-ul-lm, $U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}(v)=v^2/(4V)$, so

$$
\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\E\!\left[\frac{V_L^2}{4V}\right]
=\frac{\E[V_L^2]}{4V}
=\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}.
$$

From @eq-um-lm,

$$
\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\E\!\left[\frac{(2V-V_L)^2}{4V}\right]
=\frac{4V^2-4V\E[V_L]+\E[V_L^2]}{4V}
=\frac{4V^2-4V\mu+\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}.
$$ $\square$

## Proof of @prp-stage1-br {#sec-proof-stage1-br}

From the stage-1 payoff matrix:

- If management chooses F, labor compares $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}]$ from S with $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]$ from F; the difference is $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{ML}}$.
- If management chooses S, labor compares $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]$ from F with $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]$ from S; the difference is $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}$.
- If labor chooses F, management compares $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]$ from F with $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]$ from S; the difference is $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}$.
- If labor chooses S, management compares $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]$ from F with $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]$ from S; the difference is $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=V^2\kappa^2(1-V\lambda)^2/(4(1+V\lambda)^2)\ge 0$.

The four best responses in the proposition follow directly from these four comparisons. In particular, $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=0$ if and only if $V\lambda=1$, so management's unique best response when labor chooses S is F in the generic case and management is indifferent between F and S on the knife-edge.

## Proof of @prp-stage1-ne {#sec-proof-stage1-ne}

Inspect each cell of the stage-1 payoff matrix:

- At $(S,F)$: labor has no incentive to deviate to F iff $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}]\ge\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{ML}}\ge0$. Management has no incentive to deviate to S iff $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]\ge\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}\ge0$. By @eq-delta-m-ml, the latter condition always holds, so $(S,F)$ is a Nash equilibrium iff $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{ML}}\ge0$.

- At $(F,F)$: labor has no incentive to deviate to S iff $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]\ge\E[U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{ML}}\le0$. Management has no incentive to deviate to S iff $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]\ge\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\ge0$. Hence $(F,F)$ is a Nash equilibrium iff $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{ML}}\le0$ and $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\ge0$.

- At $(F,S)$: labor has no incentive to deviate to S iff $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]\ge\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}\ge0$. Management has no incentive to deviate to F iff $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]\ge\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\le0$. Hence $(F,S)$ is a Nash equilibrium iff $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}\ge0$ and $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\le0$.

- At $(S,S)$: labor has no incentive to deviate to F iff $\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]\ge\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}\le0$. Management has no incentive to deviate to F iff $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]\ge\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]$, i.e., $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}\le0$. By @eq-delta-m-ml, $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}\le0$ is equivalent to $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=0$, or $V\lambda=1$. Hence $(S,S)$ is a Nash equilibrium iff $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}\le0$ and $V\lambda=1$.

This proves the proposition. $\square$

## Proof of @thm-timing-eq {#sec-proof-timing-eq}

The theorem follows directly from Proposition @prp-stage1-ne. The one-deviation conditions in the four cells give the necessary and sufficient conditions for ML, immediate SS, LM, and delayed SS. Equation @eq-delta-m-ml gives $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}\ge0$, with $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{ML}}=0$ if and only if $V\lambda=1$. Therefore delayed simultaneous play $(S,S)$ cannot be a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium in the generic case $V\lambda\ne1$; on the knife-edge $V\lambda=1$, it also requires the labor condition $\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}\le0$. $\square$

## Proof of @prp-ex-ante-decomp {#sec-proof-decomp}

Starting from $R(v)\equiv U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}(v)-U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}(v)$ and taking expectation over $V_L$,

$$
\E[R(V_L)]
=
\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]-\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=
-\Delta_L^{\mathrm{LM}}.
$$

This proves the proposition.

## Proof of @prp-exact-condition {#sec-proof-exact}

Type $v$ ex post prefers to move first if and only if

$$
R(v)\le 0.
$$

By definition,

$$
R(v)\leq 0
\iff
\left(\sqrt{v}-\frac{V\kappa}{2}\right)^2\leq\frac{v^2}{4V}.
$$

Because $v>0$, the square root of the right-hand side, $\frac{v}{2\sqrt V}$, is strictly positive. Hence the preceding inequality is equivalent to

$$
\left|\sqrt{v}-\frac{V\kappa}{2}\right|
\leq
\frac{v}{2\sqrt{V}}.
$$

Expanding the absolute-value inequality gives the double inequality

$$
\sqrt{v}-\frac{v}{2\sqrt{V}}
\leq
\frac{V\kappa}{2}
\leq
\sqrt{v}+\frac{v}{2\sqrt{V}}.
$$

This proves the proposition.

## Proof of @prp-mgmt {#sec-proof-mgmt}
From @eq-eum-ml and @eq-eum-lm,

$$
\E\!\left[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}\right]=\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4},
\qquad
\E\!\left[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}\right]=\frac{(2V-\mu)^2+\sigma^2}{4V}.
$$

Therefore the condition $\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]\ge\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]$ is exactly @eq-mgmt-cond. Here $\Delta_M$ is management's direct ML-versus-LM preference gap; it is distinct from the one-deviation condition $\Delta_M^{\mathrm{SS}}\le0$ required for LM in Theorem @thm-timing-eq.

## Proof of @prp-pool {#sec-proof-ext-pool}

Both incentive constraints come from the same comparison: type $\theta_i$ must earn at least as much by staying on the pooling path as by taking its best deviation under the off-path belief $\mu=1$. Thus @eq-ul-pool-i must weakly dominate @eq-ul-dev-i. After setting $y=\sqrt{x_P}$, @eq-ich and @eq-icl become @eq-ich-quad and @eq-icl-quad.

Consider the high type's constraint. The boundary equation for $\mathrm{IC}_H$ is

$$
y^2 - \frac{\theta_H^2}{\sqrt{\Psi_0}}y + \frac{\theta_H^2}{4}=0.
$$

Its discriminant is

$$
\Delta_H
= \frac{\theta_H^4}{\Psi_0}-\theta_H^2
= \frac{\theta_H^2(\theta_H^2-\Psi_0)}{\Psi_0}.
$$

Since $q\in(0,1)$ and $0<\theta_L<\theta_H$,

$$
\Psi_0=q\theta_H^2+(1-q)\theta_L^2<\theta_H^2.
$$

Hence $\Delta_H>0$. Write

$$
s \equiv \sqrt{1-\frac{\Psi_0}{\theta_H^2}} \in (0,1).
$$

The two roots of the high-type constraint are

$$
z_{\min}=\frac{\theta_H^2}{2\sqrt{\Psi_0}}(1-s),
\qquad
z_{\max}=\frac{\theta_H^2}{2\sqrt{\Psi_0}}(1+s).
$$

Since @eq-ich-quad opens downward, the inequality holds exactly between the two roots:

$$
y\in [z_{\min},z_{\max}].
$$

The low type's constraint is handled in the same way. Its boundary equation is

$$
y^2 - \frac{\theta_L^2}{\sqrt{\Psi_0}}y
+ \frac{\theta_L^4}{4\theta_H^2}=0.
$$

The discriminant is

$$
\Delta_L
=\frac{\theta_L^4}{\Psi_0}-\frac{\theta_L^4}{\theta_H^2}
=\frac{\theta_L^4(\theta_H^2-\Psi_0)}{\Psi_0\theta_H^2}.
$$

Again, $\Psi_0<\theta_H^2$ gives $\Delta_L>0$. Thus $\mathrm{IC}_L$ defines a nondegenerate interval with roots

$$
y_{\min}=\frac{\theta_L^2}{2\sqrt{\Psi_0}}(1-s),
\qquad
y_{\max}=\frac{\theta_L^2}{2\sqrt{\Psi_0}}(1+s).
$$

Since @eq-icl-quad also opens downward, the low type's feasible set is

$$
y\in [y_{\min},y_{\max}].
$$

It follows that a pooling effort $x_P=y_P^2$ satisfies both types' incentive constraints exactly when $y_P$ lies in both intervals, which is precisely @eq-pool-intersection. If the intervals fail to overlap, no common effort can work: at least one type will have a profitable deviation, and a pure-strategy pooling PBE cannot be sustained.

It remains only to locate the two intervals relative to each other. Because $\theta_L^2<\theta_H^2$, we have $y_{\min}<z_{\min}$ and $y_{\max}<z_{\max}$. The intersection condition therefore reduces to the single boundary check

$$
z_{\min}\leq y_{\max}.
$$

Equivalently, if $r\equiv \theta_L^2/\theta_H^2$, this condition becomes

$$
\frac{1-s}{1+s}\leq r. \qquad\square
$$

## Proof of the Welfare Formulas in Section @sec-welfare {#sec-proof-welfare}
By definition, $W=U_L+U_M$.

For SS (corrected BNE):

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{SS}}]
=\E[U_L^{\mathrm{SS}}]+\E[U_M^{\mathrm{SS}}]
=\left(\mu-\frac{2V\kappa\nu}{1+V\lambda}+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{(1+V\lambda)^2}\right)
+\frac{V^3\kappa^2\lambda}{(1+V\lambda)^2}.
$$

For ML:

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{ML}}]
=\E[U_L^{\mathrm{ML}}]+\E[U_M^{\mathrm{ML}}]
=\left(\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}\right)+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{4}
=\mu-V\kappa\nu+\frac{V^2\kappa^2}{2}.
$$

For LM:

$$
\E[W^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\E[U_L^{\mathrm{LM}}]+\E[U_M^{\mathrm{LM}}]
=\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{4V}+\frac{(2V-\mu)^2+\sigma^2}{4V}
=V-\mu+\frac{\mu^2+\sigma^2}{2V}. \qquad\square
$$
